image_pattern_summary: Verified good GI portable cabin images consistently show the complete cabin exterior from a 3/4 or front angle, with corrugated GI sheet cladding clearly visible, two-tone paint (typically white upper body with blue or green lower band), barred windows, and an MS door. Cabins are photographed in real deployment or yard contexts (construction sites, outdoor yards, semi-urban settings) rather than studio backgrounds. The structural form factor — rectangular box with raised legs, slope or flat roof, and visible window/door openings — is the primary visual identifier.

reason: GI portable cabin images show the complete structure as the product — the exterior form, cladding material, window/door configuration, and paint finish are the buyer-relevant visual information.

No meaningful text is printed on the product surface that a buyer would need to read (unlike labelled equipment); phone numbers and business names painted on cabins are incidental, not product information.
OCR extraction from cabin exterior images would yield only incidental branding or client names, not structural specifications — buyers evaluate from visual form, not text on the product.
